hook.convey: everyday square corners (a ludo board, a drawing book) → such a corner is a right angle → a paper folded twice tests it

use.hi: Ludo board ke chaaron kone ek jaise square corner hote hain. Aaj dekhenge ki aise kone ko right angle kehte hain, aur use kaagaz se kaise check karte hain.
use.en: All four corners of a ludo board are the same square corners. Today we see that such a corner is called a right angle, and how to check it with paper.

use.hi: Apni drawing book ka kona dekho. Aaj ek mude hue kaagaz se check karenge ki woh kona right angle hai ya nahi.
use.en: Look at the corner of your drawing book. Today we check with a folded paper whether that corner is a right angle or not.

explain.convey: a square's corners are square corners, like a book's corner → each one is a right angle (samkon)

point.hi: Yeh ek square hai. Iska kona bilkul kitaab ke kone jaisa square corner hai. Aise kone ko right angle kehte hain, Hindi mein samkon.
point.en: This is a square. Its corner is a square corner, just like the corner of a book. Such a corner is called a right angle, samkon in Hindi.

prompt.hi: Is square ke saare kone ek jaise hain. Is square mein kul kitne right angle hain?
prompt.en: All the corners of this square are the same. How many right angles does this square have in all?

why.hi: square ke 4 kone hain aur saare ek jaise square corner hain
why.en: a square has 4 corners and all of them are the same square corners

simpler.hi: Square ka har kona kitaab ke kone jaisa square corner hai. Aisa har kona ek right angle hai, toh bas kone gino.
simpler.en: Every corner of a square is a square corner, like a book's corner. Each such corner is one right angle, so just count the corners.

explain.convey: fold a paper in half, then in half again → its corner is a square corner = the tester; put it on a corner: exact fit (no space left, no overlap) → right angle

point.hi: Kaagaz ko do baar modo, toh uska kona square corner ban jaata hai. Yeh hamara tester hai. Tester ko kone par rakho. Agar woh bilkul fit ho, na khaali jagah na overlap, toh woh kona right angle hai.
point.en: Fold a paper twice, and its corner becomes a square corner. This is our tester. Put the tester on a corner. If it fits exactly, with no empty space and no overlap, that corner is a right angle.

prompt.hi: Tester ko table ke ek kone par rakha. Kone aur tester ke beech khaali jagah reh gayi. Kya woh kona right angle hai, haan ya nahi?
prompt.en: The tester is put on a corner of a table. Some empty space is left between the corner and the tester. Is that corner a right angle, yes or no?

why.hi: tester aur kone ke beech khaali jagah bachi, toh tester bilkul fit nahi hua aur woh kona right angle nahi hai
why.en: empty space was left by the tester, so it did not fit exactly and that corner is not a right angle

simpler.hi: Do baar moda kaagaz hamara tester hai. Tester kone mein bilkul fit ho aur koi khaali jagah na bache, tabhi kona right angle hai.
simpler.en: Paper folded twice is our tester. Only if the tester fits the corner exactly, with no empty space left, is the corner a right angle.

explain.convey: the same square, once straight and once turned → turning changes where it points, not its corners → the turned square's corners are still right angles

point.hi: Yeh do ek jaise square hain. Pehla seedha rakha hai, doosra ghumaya hua hai. Ghumane se square ki jagah badli, par uske kone nahi badle.
point.en: These are two identical squares. The first is placed straight, the second is turned. Turning changed where the square sits, but its corners did not change.

prompt.hi: Ghumaye hue square ke kitne kone right angle hain?
prompt.en: How many corners of the turned square are right angles?

why.hi: ghumaya hua square wahi square hai, toh uske 4 kone ab bhi right angle hain
why.en: the turned square is the same square, so its 4 corners are still right angles

simpler.hi: Square ko ghumao toh sirf uski jagah badalti hai. Uske kone wahi rehte hain jo pehle the.
simpler.en: When you turn a square, only its position changes. Its corners stay just as they were.

problem.hi: Kya khidki ka kona right angle hai? Kaagaz ke tester se check karo.
problem.en: Is the corner of a window a right angle? Check it with a paper tester.

simpler.hi: Hamare paas ek kaagaz ka tester hai. Usse khidki ke ek kone ko jaanchna hai.
simpler.en: We have a paper tester. We use it to check one corner of a window.

givens.hi: Hamare paas ek saada kaagaz hai, aur khidki ka ek kona jaanchna hai.
givens.en: We have a plain sheet of paper, and one corner of the window to check.

find.hi: khidki ka kona right angle hai ya nahi
find.en: whether the window's corner is a right angle

do.hi: Kaagaz ko aadha modo, phir dobara aadha modo
do.en: Fold the paper in half, then in half again

why.hi: do baar modne se kaagaz ka kona bilkul square corner banta hai
why.en: folding twice makes the paper's corner an exact square corner

simpler.hi: Kaagaz ko ek baar aadha modo, phir ek baar aur. Jo kona banta hai woh square corner hai, yahi tester hai.
simpler.en: Fold the paper in half once, then once more. The corner you get is a square corner, and that is the tester.

do.hi: Tester ko khidki ke kone mein rakho
do.en: Put the tester into the window's corner

steps.result: tester bilkul fit hota hai, na khaali jagah na overlap

why.hi: tester ki dono kinaariyan khidki ki dono lines par poori baith jaati hain
why.en: both edges of the tester sit fully along both lines of the window

simpler.hi: Tester ko khidki ke kone mein rakho. Uski dono kinaariyan khidki ki lines par poori baith gayi, koi khaali jagah nahi.
simpler.en: Put the tester in the window's corner. Both its edges sit fully along the window's lines, with no empty space.

prompt.hi: Tester bilkul fit hua. Toh khidki ka kona kaunsa angle hai?
prompt.en: The tester fits exactly. So what kind of angle is the window's corner?

simpler.hi: Jo kona tester mein bilkul fit ho, woh square ke kone jaisa hai. Yaad karo, square ke kone ko humne kya naam diya tha.
simpler.en: A corner that fits the tester exactly is like a square's corner. Remember the name we gave to a square's corner.

why.hi: tester khidki ke kone mein bilkul fit hua, aur aisa kona right angle hota hai
why.en: the tester fit the window's corner exactly, and such a corner is a right angle

answer.hi: khidki ka kona right angle hai
answer.en: the window's corner is a right angle

why.hi: tester ka square corner khidki ke kone mein bilkul fit hua
why.en: the tester's square corner fitted the window's corner exactly

prompt.hi: Ek kitaab ko ghumakar tircha rakha, ab woh diamond jaisi dikhti hai. {friend} ka kehna hai ki ab uske kone right angle nahi rahe. Kya yeh sahi hai?
prompt.en: A book is turned and laid slanting, so now it looks like a diamond. {friend} says its corners are no longer right angles. Is that right?

accept: nahi, ab bhi right angle hain
no, they are still right angles

why.hi: ghumaakar rakhne se kitaab ke kone nahi badalte, woh ab bhi right angle hain
why.en: laying the book slanting does not change its corners; they are still right angles

simpler.hi: Kitaab ghumane se sirf uski jagah badalti hai. Ab socho, uske kone badle ya wahi rahe.
simpler.en: Turning the book only changes where it sits. Now think whether its corners changed or stayed the same.

prompt.hi: Ek square noticeboard diwar par diamond ki tarah latka hai. Uske kitne kone right angle hain?
prompt.en: A square noticeboard hangs on the wall like a diamond. How many of its corners are right angles?

why.hi: noticeboard square hai, aur latkaane ka tareeka uske 4 right angle kone nahi badalta
why.en: the noticeboard is a square, and the way it hangs does not change its 4 right-angle corners

simpler.hi: Noticeboard square hi hai, bas tircha latka hai. Square ke har kone ko ek-ek karke gino.
simpler.en: The noticeboard is still a square, it just hangs slanting. Count each corner of the square one by one.

prompt.hi: Ek square patang hawa mein diamond jaisi udti hai. Uske upar wale kone par tester rakho. Kya tester bilkul fit hoga, haan ya nahi?
prompt.en: A square kite flies in the air like a diamond. Put the tester on its top corner. Will the tester fit exactly, yes or no?

why.hi: patang square hai, toh diamond jaisi udne par bhi uska har kona right angle hai
why.en: the kite is a square, so even flying like a diamond each of its corners is a right angle

simpler.hi: Patang ek square hai, bas tirchi ud rahi hai. Yaad karo, ghumane se square ke kone nahi badalte.
simpler.en: The kite is a square, just flying slanted. Remember, turning a square does not change its corners.

ladder.why: make the folded tester and test a book's corner → exact fit = right angle
clock hands at 3 o'clock → up and across = square corner
6 o'clock vs 9 o'clock → only one makes a square corner
error spot: a turned book's corners → still right angles
harder: a tilted square noticeboard → tilting does not change the corner

remediation.move: tester on a square tile; turn the tile a little at a time and test again each time → the tile's position changes, the corner does not

say.hi: Ek square tile socho. Use thoda-thoda ghumao aur har baar tester lagao. Tile ki jagah badalti hai, par tester har baar bilkul fit hota hai.
say.en: Imagine a square tile. Turn it a little at a time and put the tester on it each time. The tile's position changes, but the tester fits exactly every time.

simpler.hi: Socho, tile ghumane se sirf uski jagah badalti hai. Tester phir bhi har baar bilkul fit hota hai.
simpler.en: Imagine it: turning the tile only changes where it is. The tester still fits exactly every time.

prompt.hi: Ek square rumaal ko ghumakar diamond jaisa rakh diya. Kya uske kone ab bhi right angle hain?
prompt.en: A square handkerchief is turned and laid like a diamond. Are its corners still right angles?

accept: haan, ab bhi right angle hain

why.hi: rumaal square hai, aur ghumaane se uske kone nahi badalte
why.en: the handkerchief is a square, and turning it does not change its corners

simpler.hi: Rumaal square hai, sirf ghumaya gaya hai. Ghumane se jagah badalti hai, kone nahi badalte.
simpler.en: The handkerchief is a square, only turned. Turning changes the position, not the corners.

bridgeToNext.hi: Ab tak tester se dekha ki kona fit hota hai ya nahi. Ab dekhenge ki jo kona fit nahi hota, jaise cake ki nok, woh right angle se kam khula hai ya zyada.
bridgeToNext.en: So far we checked whether a corner fits the tester. Next we see whether a corner that does not fit, like a cake's tip, opens less or more than a right angle.

simpler.hi: Ab dekha ki kona tester mein fit hota hai ya nahi. Agle hisse mein dekhenge ki jo kona fit nahi hota, woh chhota hai ya bada.
simpler.en: We saw whether a corner fits the tester. Next we see whether a corner that does not fit is smaller or bigger.

hook.convey: a pointed slice tip and a game-map angle → compare each opening with the tester → less, equal or more than a right angle; long lines do not make an angle bigger

use.hi: Kitchen mein cake ka ek slice dekho, uski nok patli hoti hai. Aaj dekhenge ki woh nok right angle se kam khuli hai ya zyada.
use.en: Look at a slice of cake in the kitchen; its tip is narrow. Today we see whether that tip opens less or more than a right angle.

use.hi: Video game ke map mein kisi angle ki lines bahut lambi ho sakti hain. Aaj dekhenge ki lambi lines se angle bada hota hai ya nahi.
use.en: On a video game map the lines of an angle can be very long. Today we see whether long lines make an angle bigger or not.

explain.convey: tester on a corner → corner narrower than the tester = less than a right angle; exact fit = equal; corner opens wider than the tester = more than a right angle

point.hi: Tester ko kone par rakho. Agar kona tester se tang hai, toh woh right angle se kam hai. Agar kona tester se zyada khula hai, toh woh right angle se zyada hai. Bilkul fit ho, toh right angle ke barabar.
point.en: Put the tester on the corner. If the corner is narrower than the tester, it is less than a right angle. If the corner opens wider than the tester, it is more than a right angle. If it fits exactly, it equals a right angle.

prompt.hi: Ek cake slice ki nok tester se tang hai. Nok ka angle right angle se kam hai ya zyada?
prompt.en: The tip of a cake slice is narrower than the tester. Is the tip's angle less or more than a right angle?

why.hi: nok tester se bhi tang hai, aur tester khud ek right angle hai
why.en: the tip is narrower than the tester, and the tester itself is a right angle

simpler.hi: Tester ko kone se milao. Kona tester se tang ho toh angle chhota hai, aur zyada khula ho toh angle bada hai.
simpler.en: Hold the tester against the corner. If the corner is narrower than the tester the angle is smaller, and if it opens wider the angle is bigger.

explain.convey: angle P: square corner with short arms; angle Q: square corner with long arms → the tester fits both → same angle; an angle is how wide the arms open, not how long they are

point.hi: Angle bhuja ki lambai se nahi, uske khulne se naapte hain. Bhuja chhoti ho ya lambi, agar tester bilkul fit hota hai, toh woh square corner hai. Yeh khulna hi angle hai.
point.en: An angle is measured by how wide it opens, not by the length of its arms. Short arms or long, if the tester fits exactly, it is a square corner. This opening is the angle.

prompt.hi: Ek kone ki bhuja 3 cm hai, doosre ki 12 cm, aur dono par tester bilkul fit hota hai. Kaunsa angle bada hai, ya dono barabar?
prompt.en: One corner has arms 3 cm long, another has arms 12 cm long, and the tester fits both exactly. Which angle is bigger, or are both equal?

why.hi: tester dono par bilkul fit hota hai, aur 3 cm ya 12 cm ki bhuja khulna nahi badalti
why.en: the tester fits both exactly, and arms of 3 cm or 12 cm do not change the opening

simpler.hi: Bhuja lambi ho ya chhoti, angle usse nahi badalta. Sirf dekho ki kona kitna khula hai.
simpler.en: Long arms or short arms, that does not change the angle. Just look at how wide the corner opens.

explain.convey: angle A: long arms, opens only a little (like scissors slightly open); angle B: short arms, a full square corner → B opens wider → B is the bigger angle

point.hi: Ek angle ki bhuja lambi ho sakti hai, par woh thoda sa hi khula ho, jaise thodi si khuli kainchi. Doosre ki bhuja chhoti ho, par woh poora square corner ho. Jo zyada khula hai, wahi bada angle hai.
point.en: One angle can have long arms but open only a little, like scissors opened slightly. Another can have short arms but be a full square corner. Whichever opens wider is the bigger angle.

prompt.hi: Ek lambi kainchi thodi si khuli hai. Ek chhoti diary ka kona square corner hai. Kaunsa angle bada hai: kainchi ka ya diary ke kone ka?
prompt.en: A long pair of scissors is opened slightly. The corner of a small diary is a square corner. Which angle is bigger: the scissors' or the diary corner's?

why.hi: lambi kainchi thodi si hi khuli hai, jabki chhoti diary ka kona poora square corner khula hai
why.en: the long scissors are open only a little, while the small diary's corner is open a full square corner

simpler.hi: Bhuja ki lambai bhool jao. Sirf dekho kaun zyada khula hai: thodi khuli cheez ya poora square corner.
simpler.en: Forget the length of the arms. Just see which opens wider: something opened a little, or a full square corner.

problem.hi: Rani ki rangoli mein 3 kone hain. Kone P ki bhuja 9 cm hai, aur woh tester ke andar reh jaata hai, beech mein khaali jagah. Kone Q ki bhuja 4 cm hai, aur tester bilkul fit hota hai. Kone R ki bhuja 3 cm hai, aur uski ek bhuja tester ke bahar jaati hai. Sabse bada angle kaunsa hai?
problem.en: Rani's rangoli has 3 corners. Corner P has arms 9 cm long and stays inside the tester, with empty space between. Corner Q has arms 4 cm long and the tester fits exactly. Corner R has arms 3 cm long and one arm goes outside the tester. Which is the biggest angle?

simpler.hi: Teen kone P, Q aur R hain. Tester se dekhkar batana hai ki inmein sabse bada angle kaunsa hai.
simpler.en: There are three corners, P, Q and R. Using the tester, we say which of them is the biggest angle.

givens.hi: Teeno kone tester se mile: P mein khaali jagah bachi, Q bilkul fit hua, aur R tester ke bahar gaya.
givens.en: All three corners met the tester: P left empty space, Q fit exactly, and R went outside the tester.

find.hi: teeno mein sabse bada angle kaunsa hai
find.en: which of the three is the biggest angle

do.hi: P aur Q ko tester se milao
do.en: Compare P and Q with the tester

steps.result: P right angle se kam, Q right angle ke barabar

why.hi: P tester se tang hai aur Q bilkul fit hota hai
why.en: P is narrower than the tester and Q fits exactly

simpler.hi: P tester se tang hai, toh P right angle se chhota hai. Q tester mein bilkul fit hai, toh Q right angle hai.
simpler.en: P is narrower than the tester, so P is smaller than a right angle. Q fits the tester exactly, so Q is a right angle.

do.hi: Ab R ko tester se milao
do.en: Now compare R with the tester

why.hi: R ki ek bhuja tester ke bahar jaati hai, yaani R zyada khula hai
why.en: one arm of R goes outside the tester, so R opens wider

simpler.hi: R ki ek bhuja tester se bahar nikalti hai. Matlab R tester se bhi zyada khula hai, right angle se bada.
simpler.en: One arm of R goes outside the tester. That means R opens even wider than the tester, more than a right angle.

prompt.hi: Ab bhuja ki lambai chhodo, sirf khulna dekho. Teeno mein sabse bada angle kaunsa hai?
prompt.en: Now ignore the arm lengths and look only at the opening. Which of the three is the biggest angle?

simpler.hi: Bhuja ki lambai mat dekho. Jo kona tester se bhi zyada khula hai, wahi sabse bada angle hai.
simpler.en: Do not look at the arm lengths. The corner that opens even wider than the tester is the biggest angle.

why.hi: P mein khaali jagah bachi, Q bilkul fit hua, par R tester ke bahar jaata hai, toh R sabse khula hai
why.en: P left empty space and Q fit exactly, but R's arm goes outside the tester, so R opens the most

answer.hi: teeno mein sabse bada angle R hai
answer.en: R is the biggest of the three angles

why.hi: R sabse zyada khula hai, aur P ki lambi bhuja se uska angle bada nahi hota
why.en: R opens the widest, and P's long arms do not make its angle bigger

prompt.hi: Angle A ki bhuja 15 cm hai, aur woh right angle se kam khulta hai. Angle B ki bhuja 3 cm hai, aur woh right angle se zyada khulta hai. Kaunsa angle bada hai, A ya B?
prompt.en: Angle A has arms 15 cm long and opens less than a right angle. Angle B has arms 3 cm long and opens more than a right angle. Which angle is bigger, A or B?

why.hi: B right angle se zyada khulta hai aur A kam, aur 15 cm ya 3 cm ki bhuja se farak nahi padta
why.en: B opens more than a right angle and A less, and arms of 15 cm or 3 cm make no difference

simpler.hi: 15 cm ki lambi bhuja se angle bada nahi hota. Sirf dekho kaun right angle se zyada khulta hai.
simpler.en: Long 15 cm arms do not make an angle bigger. Just see which one opens more than a right angle.

prompt.hi: Ek badi kitaab aur ek chhoti diary, dono ke kone square corner hain. {friend} ka kehna hai ki badi kitaab ka kona bada angle hai. Kya yeh sahi hai?
prompt.en: A big book and a small diary: each one's corner is a square corner. {friend} says the big book's corner is a bigger angle. Is that right?

why.hi: badi kitaab aur chhoti diary dono ke kone square corner hain, toh dono utne hi khule hain
why.en: the big book and the small diary both have square corners, so both open the same amount

simpler.hi: Dono ke kone square corner hain, toh dono ek jitne khule hain. Kitaab ka bada size angle nahi badalta.
simpler.en: Both corners are square corners, so both open the same amount. The book's bigger size does not change the angle.

prompt.hi: Ek angle ki bhuja 20 cm lambi hai, par woh kona tester se tang hai. Yeh angle right angle se kam hai ya zyada?
prompt.en: An angle has arms 20 cm long, but the corner is narrower than the tester. Is this angle less or more than a right angle?

why.hi: kona tester se tang hai, aur 20 cm lambi bhuja use zyada nahi kholti
why.en: the corner is narrower than the tester, and 20 cm arms do not open it any wider

simpler.hi: Bhuja kitni bhi lambi ho, angle sirf khulne se naapte hain. Ab socho, tester se tang kona right angle se chhota hai ya bada.
simpler.en: However long the arms are, an angle is measured only by its opening. Now think whether a corner narrower than the tester is smaller or bigger than a right angle.

ladder.why: predict: square corners with 2 cm and 10 cm arms → the same angle
a pizza tip narrower than a napkin corner → less than a right angle
long arms opened a little vs a short square corner → the square corner is bigger
say why longer arms do not make a bigger angle → an angle is the opening
harder contrast: 12 cm arms opening less vs 2 cm arms opening more

remediation.move: two-arm angle maker: hold the opening fixed, stretch the arms longer and longer → the opening does not change → then lay the paper tester on it

say.hi: Angle ka khulna pakad lo aur bhuja chhoti se lambi karte jao. Khulna wahi rehta hai, toh angle bhi wahi rehta hai.
say.en: Hold the angle's opening still and make its arms longer and longer. The opening stays the same, so the angle stays the same too.

simpler.hi: Bhuja lambi karo, khulna wahi rehta hai. Toh angle bhi wahi rehta hai.
simpler.en: Make the arms longer and the opening stays the same. So the angle stays the same.

prompt.hi: Do kainchi ek jitni khuli hain. Ek ki blade 5 cm, doosri ki 15 cm. Kaunsa angle bada hai, ya dono barabar?
prompt.en: Two scissors open by the same amount; one has 5 cm blades, one 15 cm. Which angle is bigger, or are they equal?

why.hi: dono kainchi ek jitni khuli hain, aur 5 cm ya 15 cm ki blade khulna nahi badalti
why.en: both scissors are opened the same amount, and 5 cm or 15 cm blades do not change the opening

simpler.hi: Blade ki lambai angle nahi badalti. Sirf dekho ki dono kainchi kitni khuli hain.
simpler.en: The blade length does not change the angle. Just look at how wide the two scissors are open.

bridgeToNext.hi: Ab tak hum kone aur angle dekh rahe the. Ab ek aisi shape dekhenge jismein koi kona hi nahi hota: circle.
bridgeToNext.en: So far we looked at corners and angles. Next we look at a shape that has no corner at all: the circle.

simpler.hi: Kone aur angle hum dekh chuke. Agle hisse mein ek aisi shape dekhenge jisme koi kona hota hi nahi, circle.
simpler.en: We have seen corners and angles. Next we meet a shape with no corner at all, the circle.

hook.convey: draw round a bangle, or mark a big circle in the playground with a rope and chalk → a circle has a centre, and every point on it is the same distance from the centre

use.hi: Ek chudi kaagaz par rakho aur uske kinaare par pencil ghumakar drawing banao. Jo shape banegi, woh circle hai. Aaj dekhenge ki circle ki khaas baat kya hai.
use.en: Put a bangle on paper and run a pencil round its edge to make a drawing. The shape you get is a circle. Today we see what is special about a circle.

use.hi: Playground mein ek game ke liye bada circle banana hai. Aaj seekhenge ki rassi aur chalk se sahi circle kaise banta hai.
use.en: A big circle is needed in the playground for a game. Today we learn how a rope and chalk make a true circle.

explain.convey: string compass: one end of the string held still at the centre, pencil at the other end, string kept tight → the pencil stays the string's length from the centre at every point

point.hi: String ka ek sira beech mein haath se dabakar rakho. Yeh point circle ka centre hai, Hindi mein kendra. Doosre sire par pencil baandho aur string tight rakhkar ghumao. Pencil har jagah centre se utni hi door rehti hai jitni string lambi hai.
point.en: Hold one end of the string still in the middle with your hand. This point is the circle's centre, kendra in Hindi. Tie a pencil to the other end and turn it with the string kept tight. Everywhere, the pencil stays as far from the centre as the string is long.

prompt.hi: Is circle ke kinaare ka ek point centre se 4 cm door hai. Kinaare ka koi doosra point centre se 4 cm se kam door hoga, zyada, ya barabar?
prompt.en: One point on the edge of this circle is 4 cm from the centre. Will another point on the edge be less than, more than, or equal to 4 cm from the centre?

why.hi: circle ke kinaare ka har point centre se ek jitna door hota hai, isliye doosra point bhi 4 cm door hai
why.en: every point on a circle's edge is equally far from the centre, so the other point is also 4 cm away

simpler.hi: String ki lambai kabhi nahi badalti. Isliye pencil har jagah centre se utni hi door rehti hai.
simpler.en: The string's length never changes. So the pencil stays the same distance from the centre everywhere.

explain.convey: bangle: every point the same distance from its centre → a circle; egg: longer one way, the distance changes → round, but not a circle

point.hi: Chudi ke centre se uska har point barabar door hai, isliye chudi circle hai. Anda ek taraf lamba hai, centre se doori badalti rehti hai. Isliye anda gol toh hai, par circle nahi.
point.en: Every point of the bangle is equally far from its centre, so the bangle is a circle. An egg is longer one way; the distance from the centre keeps changing. So an egg is round, but not a circle.

prompt.hi: Ek roti ke centre se kinaara ek taraf 8 cm hai aur doosri taraf 10 cm. Kya yeh roti circle hai, haan ya nahi?

accept: no, the distances are not equal

why.hi: roti ka kinaara centre se ek taraf 8 cm aur doosri taraf 10 cm hai, toh roti circle nahi
why.en: the roti's edge is 8 cm from the centre one way, 10 cm the other, so it is not a circle

simpler.hi: Circle mein centre se har kinaara ek jitna door hota hai. Anda ek taraf lamba hai, isliye uski doori badalti rehti hai.
simpler.en: In a circle every point of the edge is the same distance from the centre. An egg is longer one way, so its distance keeps changing.

explain.convey: playground circle: rope 3 m tied to a peg, chalk at the other end, rope kept tight → every chalk mark is 3 m from the peg; a mark at another distance is not on this circle

point.hi: Khoonte se 3 m ki rassi baandho, doosre sire par chalk. Rassi tight rakhkar chalo, toh chalk ka har nishaan khoonte se 3 m door aata hai. Isliye yeh sahi circle banta hai.
point.en: Tie a 3 m rope to a peg, with chalk at the other end. Walk round keeping the rope tight, and every chalk mark comes 3 m from the peg. That is why this makes a true circle.

prompt.hi: Is circle ke paas ek nishaan khoonte se 4 m door hai. Kya woh nishaan is circle par hai, haan ya nahi?

why.hi: is circle ka har nishaan khoonte se 3 m door hai, par woh nishaan 4 m door hai
why.en: every mark of this circle is 3 m from the peg, but that mark is 4 m away

simpler.hi: Rassi 3 m ki hai, toh har chalk nishaan khoonte se 3 m door aata hai. Circle par sirf wahi nishaan hain jo 3 m door hain.
simpler.en: The rope is 3 m long, so every chalk mark comes 3 m from the peg. Only marks that are 3 m away are on the circle.

problem.hi: Pooja rangoli ke liye 50 cm ki string ke ek sire par chalk baandhti hai. Doosra sira centre par pakadkar, string tight rakhkar circle banati hai. Phir ek kinaare se centre se hote hue doosre kinaare tak seedhi line kheenchti hai. Woh line kitni lambi hai?

simpler.hi: Ek 50 cm ki string ka ek sira centre par hai aur doosre sire par chalk hai, aur isse circle bana. Ab ek kinaare se centre se hote hue doosre kinaare tak ki line ki lambai nikalni hai.
simpler.en: A 50 cm string has one end at the centre and chalk at the other end, and it draws a circle. Now we find the length of the line from one edge, through the centre, to the other edge.

givens.hi: 50 cm ki tight string ka ek sira centre par hai, aur line centre se hokar ek kinaare se doosre kinaare tak jaati hai.
givens.en: A tight 50 cm string has one end at the centre, and the line runs from one edge through the centre to the other edge.

do.hi: Pehle dekho kinaara centre se kitni door hai

do.hi: Ab line ke dono taraf dekho, centre ke is paar aur us paar

why.hi: line centre se hokar ek kinaare se doosre kinaare tak jaati hai

simpler.hi: Line centre se hokar jaati hai. Centre ke ek taraf kinaare tak 50 cm hai, aur doosri taraf bhi 50 cm.

prompt.hi: Ab dono taraf ki lambai jodo. Poori line kitni lambi hai?
prompt.en: Now add the lengths on both sides. How long is the whole line?

prompt.hi: Ek anda gol dikhta hai. Uske centre se kinaara ek taraf 3 cm aur doosri taraf 4 cm door hai. Kya anda circle hai?
prompt.en: An egg looks round. From its centre the edge is 3 cm away on one side and 4 cm on the other. Is the egg a circle?

why.hi: ande ka kinaara centre se ek taraf 3 cm aur doosri taraf 4 cm hai, toh anda circle nahi
why.en: the egg's edge is 3 cm from the centre one way, 4 cm the other, so it is not a circle

simpler.hi: Ande ke kinaare ki doori dekho: ek taraf 3 cm, doosri taraf 4 cm. Circle mein yeh har taraf ek jitni hoti hai.
simpler.en: Look at the egg's edge: 3 cm on one side, 4 cm on the other. In a circle it is the same on every side.

prompt.en: {friend} drew a round loop by hand. From its centre the edge is 5 cm away in some places and 6 cm in others. Is this loop a circle?

why.hi: loop ka kinaara centre se kahin 5 cm aur kahin 6 cm hai, toh loop circle nahi
why.en: the loop's edge is 5 cm from the centre in places and 6 cm in others, so it is not a circle

simpler.hi: Is loop mein kahin 5 cm hai aur kahin 6 cm. Sach ke circle mein centre se doori har jagah ek jaisi rehti hai.
simpler.en: This loop has 5 cm in places and 6 cm in others. In a true circle the distance from the centre stays the same everywhere.

why.hi: chudi ka har point centre se barabar door hai, jabki anda ek taraf lamba hai
why.en: every point of the bangle is equally far from its centre, while the egg is longer one way

simpler.hi: Circle wahi hai jiska har kinaara centre se ek jitna door ho. Anda ek taraf lamba hota hai.
simpler.en: A circle is the one whose edge is the same distance from the centre everywhere. An egg is longer one way.
